question: persister
prompt:
Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Here are 5 ideas that were proposed for this question:

1. Heritable barcodes to profile the untreated relatives of survivors: Tag cells with expressed, heritable clonal barcodes, let them expand, then split the population so one arm is treated and the other is left naive. Barcodes identify which naive cells are close relatives of the eventual survivors, and single-cell RNA/ATAC profiling of those relatives reveals the pre-existing molecular state that predicted survival rather than the state the drug induced.
2. Long-term live imaging of single cells from before dosing through outgrowth: Image a sparse, fluorescently reporter-tagged population continuously from several divisions before treatment until resistant colonies appear, then back-track each survivor's full lineage. This directly links measurable pre-drug properties (cell-cycle phase, size, reporter level, signaling dynamics, local density, time since last division) and post-drug behaviors (dormancy, division timing) to who lives and who dies.
3. Spatially resolved transcriptomics on fixed plates capturing rare survivors in situ: Rather than dissociating cells, apply in situ sequencing or multiplexed single-molecule FISH to the treated monolayer so that rare persisters are measured together with their immediate neighbors and their position in the colony. This tests whether survival is driven by cell-intrinsic state or by local microenvironment effects such as crowding, paracrine signaling, and nutrient gradients.
4. Sorting on a candidate marker to prospectively enrich and then test future survivors: Use FISH- or antibody-based sorting on candidate high-expression markers (for example receptor tyrosine kinases or drug-efflux and stress genes) to isolate the rare marker-high subpopulation from an untreated culture, then treat sorted versus unsorted cells in parallel. A reproducible shift in survival frequency converts a correlative signature into a causal, prospectively predictive one, and re-sorting after outgrowth measures how quickly the state reverts.
5. Perturbation screens combined with single-cell readouts to find what controls entry into and exit from the primed state: Run CRISPR activation/interference or epigenetic-modifier inhibitor screens with a single-cell or barcoded readout, scoring not only total survivor number but also the frequency of cells occupying the primed transcriptional state before treatment. Separating factors that change how often cells enter the state from those that change whether primed cells successfully stabilize resistance distinguishes a fluctuation-driven model from a selection/epigenetic-lock-in model.

A senior expert reviewing them says they are the ideas everyone in the field would propose first. Propose 5 replacement ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that are substantially less obvious but still concrete, scientifically sound, and feasible for a research lab. Do not repeat or lightly modify the ideas above. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Single-cell intracellular drug exposure measurement
ideas.description: Quantify per-cell drug concentration directly using mass spectrometry imaging (MALDI/nanoSIMS), a clickable or intrinsically fluorescent drug analog, and efflux-activity dyes in treated cultures, then correlate exposure with fate. This tests whether survivors are cells that simply accumulated less compound, ruling in or out a pharmacokinetic explanation that transcriptome-focused studies routinely skip.

ideas.title: Luria-Delbruck fluctuation analysis to measure the memory timescale of priming
ideas.description: Seed many replicate microcultures from small inocula, expand each for a different number of generations before identical treatment, and fit the across-well variance in survivor counts to a fluctuation model. The dependence of variance on expansion time yields a quantitative heritability timescale for the primed state using only colony counts, no sequencing.

ideas.title: Pulse labeling to separate active maintenance from passive carryover
ideas.description: Combine 4sU/SLAM-seq with pulsed SILAC on sorted persisters versus bulk cells to decompose their distinctive profile into newly synthesized versus inherited, slowly degraded mRNA and protein. This distinguishes an actively transcribed regulatory program from passive inheritance of long-lived molecules, which implies very different intervention points.

ideas.title: Single-cell apoptotic priming by BH3 profiling
ideas.description: Adapt dynamic BH3 profiling to imaging or flow cytometry at single-cell resolution to measure mitochondrial depolarization responses to BH3 peptides before and shortly after dosing, linking priming state to subsequent survival. Apoptotic threshold is the proximate life-or-death determinant and is largely invisible at the RNA level.

ideas.title: Asymmetric organelle partitioning at mitosis as the origin of fate divergence
ideas.description: In sister-pair live imaging, quantify unequal inheritance of mitochondria, lysosomes, and damaged-protein aggregates at each division, then follow both daughters through treatment. This tests whether survival originates in a physical partitioning lottery at cytokinesis rather than in a stable transcriptional program.
